{
  "research_question": "How do the five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance metrics including Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": [
    "Combined",
    "ICMS Only",
    "Dim Visual Only",
    "Bright Visual Only",
    "Sham"
  ],
  "response_variables": [
    "Time-to-Target",
    "Success",
    "Path Efficiency",
    "Average Speed",
    "AD"
  ],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "The dataset contains 76,655 rows of navigation data across the five specified stimulation paradigms.",
    "Overall mean Time-to-Target is 2.81 seconds with a standard deviation of 2.08, indicating high variability in completion times.",
    "Overall Success rate is 72.95% (mean 0.73), suggesting that while most trials are successful, a significant portion fail.",
    "Path Efficiency has a mean of 0.47 with a very wide range (0.001 to 29.82), indicating substantial variation in route directness.",
    "Average Speed is 12.50 units with a standard deviation of 4.46.",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) has a mean of 0.38 and a standard deviation of 0.24, reflecting moderate variability in directional consistency.",
    "The 'Combined' paradigm accounts for the majority of observations (48,846), followed by 'ICMS Only' (11,378), 'Dim Visual Only' (9,603), 'Sham' (3,505), and 'Bright Visual Only' (3,323)."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "The 'Combined' paradigm has a sample size nearly 4.4 times larger than the next largest group ('ICMS Only'), which may dominate overall statistics if group-level means are not weighted or if variance differs significantly between groups.",
    "The extreme range in Path Efficiency (min 0.0009 to max 29.82) suggests that specific subgroups within the paradigms (likely the smaller 'Sham' or 'Bright Visual Only' groups) may exhibit outlier behaviors that skew the global mean.",
    "Without group-specific means and standard deviations, it is impossible to determine which specific paradigm yields the fastest Time-to-Target or highest Success rate; the global mean of 2.81s and 0.73 success cannot be attributed to a single condition."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "While the global statistics indicate that mice generally complete tasks within ~3 seconds with ~73% success, the high standard deviations and the dominance of the 'Combined' group in sample size prevent definitive conclusions about the efficacy of specific stimulation types (e.g., ICMS vs. Visual) on their own. The 'Combined' condition appears to be the primary driver of the observed population statistics. The wide variance in Path Efficiency suggests that navigation strategies vary drastically, potentially linked to the specific stimulation type or individual mouse variability.",
  "limitations": [
    "Group-level descriptive statistics (mean, SD, min, max) for each of the five stimulation paradigms are not provided in the artifact; only global aggregates are available.",
    "The 'Combined' paradigm comprises 63.7% of the data, creating a potential imbalance that obscures the performance characteristics of the smaller groups (Sham, Bright Visual Only).",
    "The extreme outliers in Path Efficiency (max 29.82) suggest the presence of erroneous data or extreme behavioral events that are not stratified by paradigm in the summary.",
    "No statistical tests (e.g., ANOVA, t-tests) were performed to confirm if observed differences between paradigms are statistically significant."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Compute group-wise descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, count) for each of the five stimulation paradigms for all five response variables to identify specific performance profiles. Subsequently, perform an ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test for each variable to determine if there are significant differences between the paradigms, followed by post-hoc pairwise comparisons."
}
